figures.alt: Unfinished Florida garage conversion with framed exterior wall, mineral-wool insulation, flashed window opening, and protected electrical box
figures.caption: An ADU conversion is a change of use and enclosure. Existing garage construction must be assessed against zoning, energy, structural, opening, insulation, service, and living-space requirements.
figures.before: First Question: Does Your Zoning Allow an ADU?

figures.alt: Compact framed half-bath rough-in with toilet drain stub, supply lines, vent connection, and sloped stair underside
figures.caption: Attached and detached garage conversions differ in how plumbing, ventilation, access, fire separation, services, and new room layout can be accommodated.

figures.alt: Renovation wall rough-in with organized framing, plumbing, electrical boxes, review folder, level, and tape measure
figures.caption: A permit-ready conversion keeps the rough-in visible for inspections and coordinates the work sequence before insulation, drywall, fixtures, and finishes close the walls.
